split_why: The split stays at five and three because it matches the flights (in through Krabi, home from Bangkok after the countdown). Krabi days 1 to 4 are dry land only (rafting, cooking, boat sightseeing), and the swims move to day 5.
monkeys_note: You stay in Ao Nang, where long-tailed macaques are rare in town, and the Railay boat trip on day 4 stays on the boat and the viewpoint path with no Monkey Trail or Phra Nang cave steps. The plan skips Phi Phi’s Monkey Beach, Tiger Cave Temple and any rafting-tour monkey cave stops; Bangkok has none.

route: Mui Ne 3 days, Ho Chi Minh City 5 days
split_why: The split stays at three days in Mui Ne and five in Ho Chi Minh City because the one drive each way is needed either way, and Ho Chi Minh City holds New Year’s Eve, New Year’s Day and the flight home. Mui Ne comes first with no swimming on days 1 to 4; swimming is left to the hotel pool in Ho Chi Minh City from day 5.
monkeys_note: None of the places in this plan are known for monkeys. Ta Cu Mountain and Can Gio’s Monkey Island have them, so both are left out.

split_why: Four and four because both stops need the same two domestic flights, Day 1 is mostly travel so Langkawi needs four days to give three usable ones, and Kuala Lumpur has to hold New Year’s Eve and the flight home. Langkawi comes first because its four dry-land days (no swimming on days 1 to 4) fit before the hotel pool swim on day 5.
monkeys_note: No monkey hotspot is visited. Macaques are seen near the SkyCab top-station café, so keep snacks packed away and take the SkyGlide lift, not the forest trail. Telaga Tujuh is viewed from the car park and viewpoint only, and Batu Caves is skipped.

split_why: Kept at three and five days: Coron town days are all on land (no swimming on days 1 to 4), then a ferry to El Nido, where the island-hopping swims and Nacpan fall on days 5 to 8. Hotels are good-value 3 to 4 star town hotels instead of a private-island resort.
monkeys_note: Long-tailed macaques are sometimes seen on Miniloc Island, where the Big and Small Lagoons are, so stay in the kayak and keep food sealed on the boat. The plan uses shared Tour A only and drops Tour C, whose Matinloc Shrine stop has monkeys; no monkeys are reported in Coron town, Mount Tapyas, Calauit, Taraw Cliff, Las Cabanas or Nacpan.

split_why: Most of Japan is cold in late December, so the plan stays in subtropical Okinawa. Ishigaki comes first because days 1 to 4 are the no-swim days and it has the best sightseeing without getting in the water (glass-bottom boat, Taketomi, mangrove paddling, stargazing). Naha comes second so you spend New Year’s Eve in Japan’s biggest Okinawan city, with toshikoshi soba and a midnight shrine visit, and fly home from Naha with no extra hop.
monkeys_note: There are no wild monkeys on Okinawa’s main island or on Ishigaki, so nothing in the plan needs avoiding.

route: Beijing 3 days, Zhangjiajie 2 days, Shanghai 3 days
split_why: Three days in Beijing cover the pandas at Beijing Zoo, Universal, the Forbidden City and the Great Wall with toboggan; two days in Zhangjiajie give one afternoon for Tianmen Mountain and one full day in the Avatar mountains; three days in Shanghai put Disneyland and the New Year’s Eve countdown at the end. Open-jaw flights (in to Beijing, home from Shanghai) and two direct domestic flights keep it simple.
monkeys_note: Wild macaques live in the Zhangjiajie forest (Yuanjiajie and the Golden Whip Stream trail are known for them), so the plan keeps to the Bailong elevator, Tianzi Mountain cable car and viewpoints, takes no food out in the open and skips the Golden Whip Stream walk. Beijing and Shanghai have none that visitors meet.

reason: Little variety without water activities: no karting or rafting, and most highlights are boat or snorkel trips
split_why: Without snorkelling, diving and repeated boat trips, Maafushi has about four distinct days, so one night moves to the resort, which also cuts mosquito exposure on the local island and adds the resort’s free festive events, at a higher cost.
monkeys_note: There are no monkeys anywhere in the Maldives; the only wildlife in this plan is dolphins seen from a boat.
Red colobus monkeys in Jozani Forest, which you can skip, and Sykes’ monkeys in some beach-hotel gardens. Stone Town has none.
Toque macaques and langurs are common in south-coast gardens, on hotel roofs and along the Bentota river.

reason: Mostly romantic, too few activities, shopping no different from Egypt
monkeys_note: Long-tailed macaques live in the forests and gorges and sometimes visit hotel gardens near them; beach areas see few.

reason: Not your style; replaced by the southern Vietnam route
monkeys_note: Few wild monkeys; mostly at the safari park, which you can skip.
